title: A skill that varies based on a variable

I tried to use java script and visustella's battle core, but it had zero change.

OK, so basically I'm trying to implement a mechanic that allows to boost moves. To activate it, you need to use a special skill. This skill simply uses up 1 MP and increases a variable by one point.
Then, when you use a skill, it runs a common event and nothing else. (no damage, no formulas, nothing.) It just checks the value in a variable. After that, it selects one of the four versions of that skill, which actually have formulas, animations, and other effects.
Spoiler:
screenshot
In case of this skill, using more boost points allows you to use the skill multiple times in a single turn. However, if 0 points are used, the skill won't work at all. Just in case, this system IS working, it just has a slight delay when using it. I'm just wondering is there more refined way to implement what I'm trying to do.
I mentioned that "I tried to use JavaScript and VisuStella's battle core" because I was testing out the note tag for the skill. I wanted to see if there is a way to trigger a common event before the damage calculation, hoping it would eliminate any delay. Unfortunately, it didn’t change anything. From what i understand, when using this skill it tries to preform a nonexistent formula, and only THEN preforms the common event and actual move. Engine treats those two skills as two different ones, which is why there is a delay. So, is there any way to make it more straightforward for the engine, with or without using plugins?

im fairly certain you can pull it off with visustella action sequences, but im not familiar with that version enough to be able to give concrete suggestions on how. It would be my go-to for setting this up though if i were you. you should be able to set up the skill to run its action animation and effect within a loop based on the loop variable.
ap9lsyn said:
I wanted to see if there is a way to trigger a common event before the damage calculation, hoping it would eliminate any delay. Unfortunately, it didn’t change anything. From what i understand, when using this skill it tries to preform a nonexistent formula, and only THEN preforms the common event and actual move.
Click to expand...
theres 2 issues there. yes, by default the common events of skills execute some time after the damage execution, but the other thing is that the engine *only* looks to run common events at specific times. using a script call to reserve a CE earlier wouldnt cause it to be executed earlier without changing that part of the engine.
you might be able to use a post-apply effect notetag and the engine's
script call
for forcing actions to force the skill a few times. Forcing the action worked with the equivalent setup using yanfly's battle core plugin where the current skill was interrupted for the second.
